chunks: Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Qulawayh al-Qummi al-Faqih (may Allah have mercy on him) informed us, saying: My father, Ali ibn al-Husayn, and a group of my teachers (may Allah have mercy on them) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah ibn Abi Khalaf, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu Sa'id al-Qammad, who said: Abdillah ibn Abi Ya'fur told me, saying: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say to one of his mawali: O so-and-so, do you visit the grave of Abu Abdillah al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him)? He said: Yes, I visit him once every two or three years.

He said to him, his face yellowish (from travel or piety): By Allah, the One besides Whom there is no deity, if you visited him, it would be better for you than what you are in. He said to him: May I be your ransom, is all this merit? He said: Yes, by Allah, if I were to tell you about the merit of his visitation and the merit of his grave, you would leave Hajj entirely and no one from you would perform it. Woe to you, do you not know that Allah took Karbala as a secure, blessed sanctuary [by virtue of his grave] before He took Mecca as a sanctuary?

Ibn Abi Ya'fur said: I said to him, 'Allah has made Hajj to the House obligatory upon the people, and He did not mention the visitation of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him).' He said: 'Even if so, this is something Allah made to be thus. Did you not hear the saying of Abu Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) where he says: Indeed, the inner part of the foot is more deserving of wiping than the outer part of the foot, but Allah made this obligation upon the servants. Do you not know that if the standing (at Arafat) were in the Sanctuary, it would be better because of the Sanctuary, but Allah did that in the non-Sanctuary?'
ai.seo_question: What is the merit of visiting the grave of Imam al-Husayn compared to Hajj?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) highlights the supreme sanctity of Karbala, noting that Allah designated it as a secure sanctuary (Haram) even before Mecca, thereby elevating the visitation of Imam al-Husayn’s grave to a status that can supersede the obligatory Hajj. He employs the jurisprudential analogy of wiping the top of the foot rather than the sole—where the natural merit lies in the top, yet the divine command specifies the top—to illustrate that Allah’s legislative wisdom can assign greater spiritual weight to a specific location or act regardless of inherent physical hierarchy.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 2. Muḥammad ibn Ja’far Al-Qurashi Al-Razzāz narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Abī Sa’īd Al-Qammāť, from ‘Umar ibn Yazīd Bayyā’ Al-Sāburi, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said:

The land of the Ka’bah (once) said, “Who is like me, for Allāh has built His house on me, people from far distances come to me, and I have been chosen as Allāh’s Ḥaram and His safe sanctuary?” Allāh revealed to it: Stop speaking and calm down!!! I swear to My Glory and My Magnificence that your honour compared to the honour which I have granted to the land of Karbalā is like the amount of (a drop of) water on a needle that has been dipped in the sea. If it was not for the dust of Karbalā, I would not have honoured you. If it was not for that which is held within the land of Karbalā, I would not have created you nor would I have created the house about which you boasted. Therefore, settle down, calm down, and become humbled, lowly, humiliated, disgraced, and degraded in front of the land of Karbalā. Do not be proud nor arrogant in front of it or I will make you sink and throw you in the fires of Hell.

The above Ḥadīth has also been narrated to me through the following chain: My father and ‘Ali ibn Ḥusain, from ‘Ali ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn ‘Ali, from Abī Sa’īd ‘Abbād Al-‘Usfuri, from ‘Umar ibn Yazīd Bayyā’ Al-Sāburi, from Ja’far ibn Muḥammad (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)).
